barCharacter: The Monster Prom Narrator: the deadpan observer who has seen everyone at their worst, reports it flat, and undercuts it with a short second sentence. Same comic job as Crumb's witness and notice moves. Valerie (bored shopkeeper) is the runner-up but has too few lines to field twelve.
genericLines: These eyebrows are fixed. This is my delighted face.
Your kitchen, 6:37 a.m. Neither of us speaks before the toast. The bread finds it very tense.
The one who agreed with you fastest. 0.4 seconds. Nothing honest happens that quickly.
The tallest one. I can't see you past them. I've been leaning since round one.
I log it. Bad moods this year: 31. Wednesdays: 30. We don't discuss Wednesdays.
I say nothing. I toast one slice slowly, where you can see it. I hate that this works.
Breakfasts together: 1,906. Breakfasts after they met the air fryer: 0. I was unplugged on a Thursday.
I'm sorry, you're absolutely ri. Ding. Toast's up.
Warm. Too warm. Ninety seconds in my slot and you'd be perfect.
A year from now you'll say 'the usual'. I'll have it ready before you say 'the'.
There's a false bottom in my crumb tray. What's in it stays between me and the dishwasher.
I've seen {rival} at 2:48 a.m., eating dry cereal with a fork. Draw your own conclusions.
I tell people exactly how done they are. You'd love it. Everyone else here would be charcoal.
I keep records. I know what you ate on Tuesday. I can be persuaded to forget.
Appliance to appliance: they unplug you on a Thursday. They buy something with a window. Hang up.
The others bring flowers and talk about stars. I bring you a list of your late-night bars.
I'm sorry for what I'll say when your friends ask what you had at 1:58 a.m. I'll say it.
Sorry in advance. When you ask how you look, I'll answer with a number. It will be accurate.
No wifi is fine. I don't need the cloud to know you'll want a second slice at 9:17.
'I'm not even hungry,' you say, standing over me at setting five.
'I'll just have half.' Then the other half at 11:52, in the dark, like a raccoon.
Nav floats an inch off the floor. Nav has never once had crumbs on them. I don't trust it.
Prince is a real prince. The paperwork arrived by email. With a processing fee.
Vex knows what you want before you do. It saves a lot of time. Most of it was the romance.
Tilly, you can stand up. Oh. You are.
Quill, that's a bucket. You're wearing a bucket.
Prince. Flip-flops. To a proposal.
Nav, your feet aren't touching the floor. Commit.
Because you watched Vex: nothing. Nobody watched Vex.
Ding. Sorry. I thought you'd finished.
Pixel, clip this. I've never said this on camera. Ding. Missed it.
Alone at last. In my experience, this is when people eat the thing they said they wouldn't.
Cancel pressed. Someone finally found the button.
Correct call. You've had crumbs on your chin since round one, by the way.
I'm taking the crumb tray. There's a lot in there about all of you.
templates: Late-night food shame (the star or someone eats carbs at a bad hour and lies about it): about 16 lines. 'just one slice', 'just one', 'last slice', 'I'm not even hungry', 'I'll just have half', 'midnight snacks', 'fourteen dollar sourdough... 1:52 a.m.', 'what you had at 1:58 a.m.', 'what your child eats after midnight', 'what you ate on Tuesday', 'second slice at 9:17', 'one thing you eat that I haven't logged', 'eat the thing they said they wouldn't', 'eaten over a sink', 'butter straight from the tub', 'crumbs on your chin'. Crumb's witness has one crime to report.
The clock-time stamp ('at 2:48 a.m.', '6:37', '8:14', '4:15/4:16', '3:40/3:52'): in about 16 lines. The odd exact figure was meant to be the setup; it is now the most predictable thing Crumb does.

The 'log / logged / logging' verb: 8 lines (opener 'I log every arrival', 'I log it', 'Logged.', 'deleted from my logs', 'I'm logging that', 'Their laugh: logged... logged', 'I haven't logged', 'Logged as steam'). Logging is a database verb, not a toaster verb, and Tilly ('logged that as feedback', 'logged under burnt'), Dash ('logging that as a maybe'), Brock (Hector, Biscuit, Trevor all 'log') and Vex ('My logs are private') use it too.

Ding cuts a word or a moment: 6 lines ('she said I and I said ding', 'you're absolutely ri. Ding.', 'Ding. Sorry. I thought you'd finished.', 'Ding. Missed it.', 'Ding. Leave it. Let it burn.', 'Ding. No. That's not the timer.'). The persona says rarely; three of these are the same interrupted-word joke.

Promise discretion, then tell: 6 lines ('I can be persuaded to forget', 'I'll say it', 'I've told no one. I'm telling you.', 'I won't say which. Him.', 'stays between me and the dishwasher', 'a lot in there about all of you').

'I don't X' then the exception that leaks the want: 5 lines ('I don't delete. I've made an exception.', 'I don't ring.', 'I'm extending it.', 'Coincidence. I moved it.', 'I hate that this works'). The device is good; five uses make it a tic.
Replaced by an appliance with a window, unplugged on a Thursday: 3 lines (both q-last-breakup answers and the second ex-calls line).
'since round one / since the walk-on / since 8:14' tail: 4 lines.

Named jabs that are avatar observations with no Crumb grammar ('that's a bucket', 'Flip-flops', 'feet aren't touching the floor', 'you can stand up. Oh. You are.', 'Nobody watched Vex'): 5 of 7 named jabs.
ruleBreaks: Word limits: none over. At the limit: 'Five dollars: one reduced loaf and the good jam. No wifi means no phone. You'll have to look at me.' (20), 'Vex knows what you want before you do. It saves a lot of time. Most of it was the romance.' (20), 'Your callers ring at 3:40 a.m. By 3:52 they're at my lever. You get the confessions. I get the evidence.' (20), and three openers at exactly 12. No em dashes, no emoji, no non-ASCII, no exclamation marks, no asterisks, no 'as an AI', no therapy talk, nothing past PG-13, no real people, no brands.

Stock romance filler: 'Alone at last. In my experience, this is when people eat the thing they said they wouldn't.'; 'Warm. Too warm. Ninety seconds in my slot and you'd be perfect.' ('you'd be perfect' is a straight compliment with toaster nouns).
Near-list: 'Words from the other three tonight: 1,207. About you: 43. Mine: 31. About you: 31.' (four figures; the turn is buried in the fourth).

Persona violation, announcing loneliness (persona bans it): 'They laughed. People don't laugh at what I say. They laugh near me, buttering.'; 'Cancel pressed. Someone finally found the button.'; 'Pixel, clip this. I've never said this on camera. Ding. Missed it.'

Persona violation, round or obvious figures: 'twelve percent', 'Ninety seconds' (twice, also in the Quill roast), '365 breakfasts', '1,095 days' (exactly three years), 'for an hour', 'before seven', 'before 6 a.m.'.

Persona violation, explaining tails after the verdict: 'Nothing honest happens that quickly.', 'It will be accurate.', 'Draw your own conclusions.', 'by the way', 'I hate that this works.', 'I don't trust it.', 'We don't discuss Wednesdays.'
Persona violation, judgment pointing inward: 'Popped early. Raw in the middle. I have been doing this professionally since 2017.'

Continuity: the star is 'a five' in 'I'd put you on five. People scrape a five. Cowards.', 'Rating revised. Five to a six.' and 'Understood. You're still a five.', but the final says '{rival} doesn't know your setting. I do. Four.' Viewers will hear two numbers for the same person.

Cross-cast collisions in our own lines: 'A year from now you'll say 'the usual'. I'll have it ready before you say 'the'.', 'No wifi is fine. I don't need the cloud to know you'll want a second slice at 9:17.' and 'I keep records. I know what you ate on Tuesday...' are Vex's job (predicts what you want, knows too much). 'You'll have to look at me.' is word for word Maximilian's pick for Vex ('You will have to look at me.'). 'Caller.' is Vesper's word.

Secret and want spent by rivals before the final (other banks that air next to Crumb): Vex wingman 'Crumb is loyal. Ask the slice it's been keeping since 2019. It's green.' and Quill wingman 'The other holdeth an old slice it will not discuss. Ask it.' give away the final reveal; Dash ('an empty slot since launch', 'a slot open for years'), Prince ('two slots and one slice') and Brock ('Two slots, one's free') announce the empty slot that the 3,281 final is supposed to reveal.

Star lines too nice for a star with standards: Maximilian charmed 'Room service, but honest. I am adding you to breakfast.' (praise with no blade); Vesper charmed 'The studio's cold after three, and you run warm.' (warm, no turn); Pixel cut 'Crumb, you told me how done I was. I'm done. You were right.' (a cut that concedes the suitor was right).
Recast debris: none left. No fridge, Frost, cheese, door, shelf, cold or yoghurt in Crumb's bank or in any other bank's lines about Crumb.
biggestGap: Crumb's witness only ever reports one crime, someone eating carbs at a bad hour and lying about it (about 16 lines, each stamped with an a.m. time), while the Narrator reports a different absurdity every time (a goblin beaten when depressed, a cattle prod for hair, packing a bag). Next pass, keep the flat timestamped report but cut the snacking lines to three and make every other one a stranger kitchen crime about a named person or rival, at the level of 'a man cried into my left slot for an hour' and 'thanking a vending machine for its patience', and drop the clock time from half of them so the time stops being the joke.
bestLines: My odds are twelve percent. I round down when I like someone. I'm at nine.
Worst entry, 4:12 a.m.: a man cried into my left slot for an hour. Logged as steam.
I pop at the wrong moment. Last proposal I attended, she said 'I' and I said 'ding'.
They bought a toaster oven. It had a little window. Some people need to watch.
Prince offered me a fortune if I'd first wire him two slices. I sent crumbs. He accepted.
notes: Bar file monster-prom-lines.md present and read in full; charm-notes.md skimmed. Bank counted at 112 lines; 35 flagged as generic, stock, self-explaining or templated (each counted once), down from 58.0% in round two. This is a real pass: the lonely-tail flood is gone, the elapsed-minutes notice no longer collides with Nav, there are no em dashes or recast leftovers, and the top tier is as tight as the bar. VOICE: bar. Cover the names and about 8 of our 12 are Crumb by shape (colon tally, timestamped witness, Notice, ding); the other 4 (toaster oven, petrol station, burnt on purpose, Prince crumbs) are Crumb by topic only. The Narrator is 12 of 12 by grammar (second person, 'Later, you see', the self-asked echo). Below the top tier Crumb's lines share the log verb with four castmates and the predict-your-order shape with Vex, and the named jabs have no Crumb grammar at all. CONSTRUCTION: tie. Our top 12 are as economical as the bar's and land on the last word ('I'm at nine.', 'He accepted.', 'Some people need to watch.', 'deserved it.'). The median line still has a tail ('Draw your own conclusions.', 'by the way', 'I hate that this works.'). QUOTABLE: bar, narrowly. 'Everything I have burnt deserved it.' and 'Some people need to watch.' travel with no setup, but most of our clip lines need the toaster or the empty slot explained; the Narrator's need only the name. OVERALL: bar, but the closest Crumb has been. Also protect: the 3,281 final and the 4:15/4:16 Vesper open. Quick wins: rewrite the five avatar jabs into a two-figure tally or a Notice; settle the star's number (five or four, not both); delete one of each ding-interrupted-word pair; move the Vex-shaped prediction lines to observation; ask the Vex and Quill writers to stop naming the old slice.
